analysis.title: Up and Adam: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
key_insights: About 30 million voters have already cast early ballots, equal to 65% of total early votes in the 2022 midterms. Among states reporting party registration, Democrats account for an average 47% of early votes versus 35% for Republicans, a 12% net Democratic advantage, up from 8.7% in 2022.

Democrats lead early voting in most, though not all, of the key Senate battleground states. Early voting tallies do not guarantee final outcomes, but the data points to stronger Democratic enthusiasm this cycle.

The Russell 1000 Value Index is outperforming the Russell 1000 Growth Index by about 22% YTD, near its strongest level since July. Energy and Utilities have led MTD gains, while Communication Services and Tech are negative MTD.

Upcoming results from Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft could help growth stocks regain relative ground versus value. The firm expects guidance to matter more than headline earnings for investor sentiment.
The US-Iran conflict reaches its nine-month mark on October 28. Officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey met Iranian counterparts to discuss a plan that could lead to a diplomatic settlement.

There are concerns the US could resume airstrikes after the midterms, which helps explain why WTI closed above $100/barrel the last two days. The White House will likely weigh regional views before acting.
Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% through October 17 versus the same period in 2025, per NielsenIQ. Candy and gum prices have risen 44% over five years, nearly twice as fast as overall food prices.
Affordability frustrations are a key reason the firm is negative on Consumer Staples. Consumer surveys point to aggregate holiday spending rising YoY.

Black Monday and Black Tuesday of 1929 erased 25% of the Dow's value and remain the only consecutive US equity days with losses over 10% each. The Dow took more than 24 years to reach a new record high but has since returned about 11.8% annualized.
